newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PSE head says sees watchdog draft by mid-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Czech PSE head says sees watchdog draft by mid-Feb.

text.p: A draft law on creating an independent Czech market securities watchdog should be ready by February 21, and presented to parliament by mid-March, Prague Stock Exchange Chairman Tomas Jezek said on Wednesday.
"July 1 was the estimated time to start it, but if it's August, September, October, that's fine. We just want it as soon as possible," he told a news conference.
Jezek, a former chairman of the parliamentary budget committee, has been working with a group of legislators to prepare legislation to establish a securities commission styled after the U.S. SEC.
"The commission will have strong authority to fine and stop trades immediately," he added.
Czech analysts have long complained about insufficient oversight on the nascent markets where transparency of stock prices and the disclosure of investor and company information is often lacking.
Since becoming PSE chairman last April, Jezek has repeatedly called for an independent watchdog which would be financed through a fee charged on every transaction.

The Czech government, which has been slow to move on the issue, said in December that it would support the eventual creation of an independent body to supervise local financial markets, possibly having the body operating by the end of the year.

Government ministers agreed with capital market experts to move supervision of the securities' markets out of the Finance Ministry into a separate "Securities Bureau" which would eventually evolve into an independent body akin to the SEC.
Despite the government's plans, Jezek has pushed forward with his preparations saying he would like the organisation to be established sooner, and apart from the Finance Ministry.
